topic: Aggregate-support pruning and boundary-safe sharp correlation-cone envelopes for imperfect-IV effects. Observe i.i.d. finite-valued treatment and instrument cells with bounded potential outcomes, consistency, SDC or SDC+LEI, and Ban-Kedagni aggregate support equality Supp(Y_d|D=d)=Supp(Y_d|D!=d)=[l_d,u_d], with no cross-arm restriction. For each sign branch form the compact missing-cell completion polytope and define tau as the maximum total interior slack. Prove a branch admits aggregate-support completion iff tau>0; unrestricted nonnegative-cone duals give its sharp arm-mean closure, and conditional product coupling gives the sharp ATE closure. Compute feasibility, tau, and endpoints by finite LPs or certified two-dimensional cone-arrangement enumeration. Prove the supplied rational four-cell example has sharp closure [711/1100,911/1100], strictly inside the published normalized outer union. For the explicit three-cell SDC family, prove disappearance of a branch makes the mean and ATE set maps Hausdorff-discontinuous and yields a 0.15 two-point minimax Hausdorff-risk lower bound. Construct a Hoeffding projection region over cell masses and bounded outcome-mass moments with finite-sample simultaneous coverage of the whole exact set. Credit Ban-Kedagni for validity and earlier cone discussion, Park for the different MIV+MTR problem, and generic mathematical-program inference; do not claim an LEI boundary from the SDC witness, clustered/covariate inference, empirical sign reversal, or unrestricted contraction. Ban-Kedagni NLSYM and Zhanhan Yu PM2.5 applications are same-population-restriction consumers whose reported object changes from a valid normalized outer region to the exact support-filtered set with a boundary diagnostic. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Fresh derivations reduced each branch to a bounded completion polytope, proved unrestricted-cone endpoint duality and aggregate BOS eligibility iff tau>0, constructed full-support endpoint approximations, and established simultaneous arm completion by conditional product coupling. Exact rational and LP calculations recovered [711/1100,911/1100] versus [0.496024,0.872824]; 72 further primal-dual arrangement checks passed. The three-cell SDC experiment was enumerated on both arms, its tilted density was shown positive for |epsilon|<3/110, and total-variation control yielded the 0.15 two-point Hausdorff-risk bound. Structural zeros, empty branches, ties, degenerate LEI variance, and score scaling were checked; no specific support-pruned collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: No theorem-critical bottleneck remains at subfield scope; production work must certify exact feasibility and tau=0 decisions near degeneracy while preserving the fixed-grid, aggregate-support, and SDC-only boundary claims. EARLY KILL TEST: Recompute the three-cell branches at epsilon=-0.001,0,0.001 and both product-coupled arms; stop if an implementation retains mean 0.3 at epsilon=0 under aggregate BOS, claims uniform shrinking along positive epsilon_n=o(1/n), or labels this witness as LEI. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_imperfectiv_sharp_cone.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Does Ban–Kédagni aggregate bounded-support equality make the SDC arm-mean and ATE regions strictly sharper than their published normalized intersection bounds, and what is the exact closure when a sign branch is support-feasible?

source_refs.claim: The paper equates factual and counterfactual supports but explicitly states that it has no proof that the resulting SDC bounds are sharp.
source_refs.author: Kyunghoon Ban and Désiré Kédagni

source_refs.claim: Park derives sharp arm-mean and ATE bounds under the distinct MIV-plus-MTR model, which does not settle sharpness under SDC and aggregate support equality.
source_refs.author: Kyungtae Park

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ban and Kédagni optimize normalized intersection expressions while aggregate support equality is an existential restriction on missing-cell distributions, not merely a box restriction on their means. Resolving sharpness requires characterizing which sign branches admit full-support completions and optimizing over the unrestricted nonnegative correlation cone. Park's argument instead uses MIV-plus-MTR order inequalities and supplies neither the required completion criterion nor the SDC cone duality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A branchwise feasibility-and-closure theorem, finite LP or cone-dual formulas for every sharp arm-mean endpoint, and a simultaneous-completion theorem showing that the sharp ATE closure is the difference of jointly attainable arm closures.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from questionable IV validity to interpretable correlation restrictions, bounded outcomes, computable ATE regions, and empirical consequences.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Perfect IV validity is often implausible -> same-direction correlation supplies a transparent relaxation -> bounded support yields computable outer regions -> aggregate support equality raises the unresolved sharpness question

method_exemplars.technique: Construct compatible arm-specific latent outcomes and prove simultaneous attainment of ATE extrema instead of subtracting marginal outer bounds without a joint witness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It closes the analogous gap between sharp arm bounds and a sharp ATE, although its order constraints must be replaced by SDC cone and support-completion constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Bootstrap randomly perturbed linear-program value functions and use LP regularity to derive inference for their linear projections.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired endpoints are LP value functions of observable moments; the additional obstacle is support-feasibility branch selection.

open_problems.open_problem: Can confidence regions for the entire exact support-filtered imperfect-IV effect set remain uniformly valid when a completion branch appears or disappears at zero interior slack?

source_refs.claim: Ban and Kédagni conduct inference for intersection-bound outer formulas, not for an exact set whose support-eligible branches can change discontinuously.
source_refs.author: Kyunghoon Ban and Désiré Kédagni

source_refs.claim: Calibrated projection gives uniformly valid intervals for smooth projections in fixed finite moment-equality and moment-inequality models.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: The ordinary bootstrap generally fails for merely directionally differentiable maps, requiring derivative-aware resampling.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing intersection-bound and calibrated-projection procedures treat fixed systems of moment restrictions. Aggregate support equality first filters branches using strict interior feasibility; at zero slack an entire component of the identified set may disappear. This is more singular than an ordinary max-min kink: plug-in Hausdorff consistency can fail along local sequences, so a valid procedure must cover the primitive observable law before applying the discontinuous exact-set map and must quantify the unavoidable loss near the boundary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample or uniformly asymptotic whole-set coverage theorem for a primitive-moment projection region, paired with a local minimax Hausdorff-risk lower bound and an away-from-boundary shrinking-rate theorem indexed by the interior-slack margin.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from partial identification to projection inference and computational feasibility, then isolate branch disappearance as the additional nonregularity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Moment restrictions identify a set -> applications require inference on causal projections -> calibrated feasibility relaxation gives uniform coverage in fixed models -> support-eligibility changes create a discontinuous-set boundary

method_exemplars.technique: Invert relaxed studentized moment constraints and compute projection endpoints through repeated feasibility optimization calibrated to the target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each imperfect-IV branch is a finite moment polytope and the ATE is a projection, but calibration must cover the union after support-feasibility filtering.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze directional derivatives of nonsmooth value maps and replace the inconsistent ordinary bootstrap with derivative-aware resampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Cone-envelope endpoints are nonsmooth LP value functions; this handles their regular boundary behavior while clarifying why branch disappearance requires additional analysis.

open_problems.open_problem: Under SDC plus the less-endogenous-instrument restriction, what is the exact aggregate-support-filtered effect set when a potential-outcome variance vanishes or a standardized correlation-cone face becomes binding?

source_refs.claim: Nevo and Rosen introduce same-sign and less-endogenous correlation restrictions and derive analytic bounds in a parametric constant-effect model.
source_refs.author: Aviv Nevo and Adam M. Rosen

source_refs.claim: Ban and Kédagni extend SDC and LEI to heterogeneous bounded potential outcomes but leave the general sharpness question unresolved.
source_refs.author: Kyunghoon Ban and Désiré Kédagni

open_problems.why_unsolved: For nondegenerate potential outcomes, the common outcome standard deviation can cancel from the LEI comparison and yield standardized linear wedges in missing-cell moments. At a degenerate potential outcome, correlation coefficients are undefined and closure conventions become substantive. An SDC-only boundary witness therefore cannot establish an LEI boundary result: new work must characterize the LEI wedge-cone dual, full-support completion on its faces, and which discontinuities are genuine rather than artifacts of division by zero.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact branchwise LP and cone-dual characterization for SDC-plus-LEI with an explicit zero-variance convention and a theorem classifying closure, one-sided limits, and branch loss at every degenerate standardized-correlation boundary.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its economic interpretation of an invalid but less endogenous instrument while making the nonparametric variance-degenerate boundary the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Perfect exclusion is doubtful -> correlation direction remains interpretable -> relative endogeneity can tighten effects -> heterogeneous bounded outcomes require an exact boundary-safe LEI characterization

method_exemplars.technique: Express SDC-plus-LEI as alternative signed standardized moment systems and optimize bounded missing outcomes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the precise LEI restrictions whose unrestricted dual and support-completion geometry must be sharpened.

method_exemplars.technique: Use directional derivatives and derivative-aware resampling for nonsmooth maps at binding inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Away from zero variance, LEI endpoints are nonsmooth optimization maps; this supplies an inference route after the more singular zero-variance regime is classified separately.

open_problems.open_problem: What are the sharp covariate-adjusted SDC imperfect-IV bounds when aggregate support equality holds conditionally and support-feasible sign branches vary across baseline-covariate values?

source_refs.claim: The paper explicitly drops exogenous covariates for simplicity, leaving conditional support completion and covariate aggregation outside its analysis.
source_refs.author: Kyunghoon Ban and Désiré Kédagni

source_refs.claim: Levis et al. derive covariate-assisted sharp IV bounds and influence-function estimators for the valid binary-IV Balke–Pearl model, not imperfect-IV SDC.
source_refs.author: Alexander W. Levis, Matteo Bonvini, Zhenghao Zeng, Luke Keele, and Edward H. Kennedy
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditioning is not a mechanical repetition of the unconditional finite-cell LP. Factual and counterfactual supports may vary with covariates, and sign branches may be feasible only on subsets of covariate space. Integrating pointwise endpoints is therefore unjustified until measurable joint completions and branch selections are established. Levis et al. supply nuisance-robust machinery for nonsmooth covariate-assisted valid-IV bounds, but their response-type polytope contains neither SDC correlation cones nor strict aggregate-support eligibility.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A measurable conditional-completion theorem yielding sharp conditional arm-mean bounds and marginal ATE endpoints as integrals of covariate-indexed LP values, plus a cross-fitted estimator with an explicit limit law under stated overlap and branch-margin conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its framing that baseline covariates can tighten IV bounds in observational applications but create nonsmooth bound functionals needing dedicated estimation theory.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: IV assumptions may be too strong -> partial bounds remain credible -> baseline covariates can tighten those bounds -> imperfect-IV SDC needs a support-safe covariate-assisted analogue

method_exemplars.technique: Translate same-direction correlation into arm-specific moment inequalities and optimize bounded missing outcomes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the donor restrictions; the first changed proof step replaces one completion polytope with a measurable field of covariate-indexed polytopes.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive influence-function estimators for expectations of nonsmooth conditional bound maps under a margin condition, with flexible nuisance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired marginal SDC endpoint is likewise an expectation of a nonsmooth conditional optimization value, augmented by branch-feasibility indicators.

open_problems.open_problem: What are the sharp marginal-potential-outcome, distributional-treatment-effect, and quantile-effect bounds under SDC and aggregate support equality with an imperfect instrument?

source_refs.claim: Ban and Kédagni derive imperfect-IV SDC bounds for potential-outcome means and average effects, not sharp marginal CDF or treatment-effect-distribution bounds.
source_refs.author: Kyunghoon Ban and Désiré Kédagni

source_refs.claim: Lee derives Makarov-based conditional treatment-effect-distribution bounds and uniform inference under different stochastic-dominance restrictions.
source_refs.author: Sungwon Lee

source_refs.claim: Kim studies marginal and joint potential-outcome distributions under triangular-model stochastic restrictions, not the SDC aggregate-support model.
source_refs.author: Ju Hyun Kim

open_problems.why_unsolved: SDC constrains selected first moments of missing potential-outcome distributions, so the finite-dimensional mean-completion dual does not directly produce extremal CDFs. Aggregate support equality also requires admissible distributions to approach all required support points, while the distribution of individual effects introduces a second optimization over unknown cross-arm dependence. Existing Makarov and transport arguments start from known or already bounded marginal distributions under different endogeneity restrictions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Sharp arm-specific CDF envelopes under SDC and aggregate support equality, followed by sharp Makarov or optimal-transport bounds for the CDF and quantiles of the individual effect Y1 minus Y0 and a uniform confidence band for the resulting bound functions.

writing_exemplar.why: Adopt its argument that mean effects conceal policy-relevant heterogeneity and that marginal counterfactual uncertainty must be separated from unknown cross-arm dependence.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average effects conceal heterogeneous gains and losses -> individual-effect distributions require marginal counterfactual laws and their dependence -> Makarov bounds separate those layers -> imperfect-IV SDC needs sharp support-filtered marginal inputs

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize marginal and joint potential-outcome distributions under integral stochastic restrictions and propagate them to treatment-effect-distribution bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the same hierarchy of marginal CDFs, joint laws, and effect distributions; the first changed step replaces triangular restrictions with SDC moment cones and aggregate-support completion.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Makarov operators to estimated potential-outcome CDF envelopes and use directional derivatives for uniform bootstrap confidence bands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once sharp SDC arm-CDF envelopes exist, the target treatment-effect-distribution map has the same max-min convolution structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate support-restricted treatment-effect-distribution bounds as an optimal-transport linear program and derive a dual representation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Aggregate support equality is a support restriction and the desired effect distribution is an extremum over cross-arm couplings.

literature_map:
Ban and Kédagni (2022, The Econometrics Journal, arXiv:2109.14785) are the central anchor: SDC, LEI, bounded aggregate support, intersection-bound inference, and an NLSYM returns-to-schooling application.
Ban and Kédagni explicitly state that they do not have a proof that their SDC bounds are sharp.
Nevo and Rosen (2012, Review of Economics and Statistics, doi:10.1162/REST_a_00171) supply the parametric same-direction and less-endogenous-instrument origin.
Manski and Pepper (2000, Econometrica) and Manski and Pepper (2009, The Econometrics Journal) are the older MIV anchors; their order restrictions are stronger and structurally different from SDC.
Park (2025, SSRN 5131175) proves sharp arm-mean and ATE bounds for MIV-plus-MTR but does not occupy the SDC aggregate-support problem.
Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013, Econometrica, arXiv:0907.3503) provide intersection-bound estimation and inference.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica, arXiv:1601.00934) provide uniformly valid calibrated projection through repeated feasibility programs for fixed moment models.
Cho and Russell (2024, JBES, arXiv:1810.03180) bootstrap perturbed LP value functions; their regularity conditions leave zero-slack branch selection as a distinct issue.
Fang and Santos (2019, Review of Economic Studies, arXiv:1404.3763) establish ordinary-bootstrap failure for merely directionally differentiable maps.
Levis et al. (2025, JRSSB, arXiv:2301.12106) develop covariate-assisted valid-IV bounds and influence-function estimation, while Ban and Kédagni explicitly omit covariates.
Lee (2024, Journal of Applied Econometrics, arXiv:2108.00723) develops conditional treatment-effect-distribution bounds and uniform inference.
Ju Hyun Kim's distributional and support-restricted treatment-effect papers (arXiv:1411.2056 and arXiv:1410.5885) supply stochastic-restriction and optimal-transport machinery, but not SDC completion.
Zhanhan Yu's PM2.5 application uses Ban–Kédagni-style same-population restrictions, illustrating that exact support filtering could change a reported empirical region.
The scan found no paper combining aggregate support equality, unrestricted SDC cone duality, strict branch-interiority diagnostics, sharp simultaneous arm coupling, and boundary-uniform whole-set inference.
